A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial rewriting and layout changes.

before.justification: v3.pdf reports original LLM fine-tuning experiments, forgetting measurements, prediction results, replay comparisons, and downstream evaluations, including appendix results.

after.justification: v4.pdf retains original LLM experiments and adds binary-forgetting evaluation, model-family and size comparisons, and controlled Rotated-MNIST experiments.

M1.justification: v4 adds logistic matrix factorization with sigmoid outputs and cross-entropy loss for binary forgetting (Section 3.1), extending the continuous formulation in v3. The matrix-completion and weighted-replay framework remains intact; renaming SVD to MF does not itself establish a new method.

E1.justification: v4 adds OLMo2-Mix and Pile as upstream evaluation corpora and introduces Rotated-MNIST digit classification with overlapping and disjoint rotation scenarios (Section 2.2 and Appendix F). The existing LLM task collections and downstream benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: v4 adds online/offline Additive-based replay comparisons and a random-guess reference for binary forgetting. The additive-versus-multiplicative fitting comparison in v3 Figure 3(a) disappears. SVD corresponds to MF; MIR is presented as task-level MIR-T, but v3's description is insufficient to establish whether its implementation changed.

E3.justification: v4 adds exact-match/F1 evaluation, model configurations extending to 13B parameters, a matched 19-task/10,000-example comparison, and controlled rotation/depth protocols. Appendix B changes prediction training from 100 to 1,000 epochs; the stated Dolma sample count changes from 141,816 to 141,876. These are reported setting revisions, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 substantially expands analysis of what determines association complexity: Figure 4 compares model families and sizes, while Appendix F varies rotation overlap and MLP depth. Binary-forgetting approximation curves are also added. Conversely, v3's direct additive-versus-multiplicative diagnostic is removed.

E5.justification: Appendix B drops v3's claim that Table 2 reports standard deviations; neither displayed table actually includes them. The domain z-test description expands from more forgetting to more or less forgetting. Single-run collection, ten seed-set repetitions, and paired t-test thresholds remain unchanged; increased replication is not established.

E6.justification: v4 adds binary prediction scores, including MF's 57.35 in-domain F1, plus model-scaling, Rotated-MNIST, and Additive-replay results. Table 2 removes Instruct-LoRA RMSE columns and changes one Similarity score from 42.38 to 42.37. Table 6 swaps OLMo-1B/7B attributions and changes StackOverflow from more to less forgotten. Most shared prediction scores and Tables 1, 4, and 5 are retained.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 adds a formal logistic factorization and cross-entropy objective for binary forgetting, extending v3's continuous formulation. The continuous low-rank mathematics is largely equivalent despite changed notation. No substantial theorem or proof development is added.

C1.justification: The central claims about low-rank associations, matrix-completion prediction, and targeted replay remain. v4 extends the claimed empirical scope from 1B/7B models to 1–13B and adds the main finding that association complexity is greater in newer, more capable families and stays stable or increases with model size.

C2.justification: v4 adds interpretations linking association complexity to shared knowledge, upstream coverage, and model depth (Appendix F), and reverses the StackOverflow interpretation alongside Table 6's model reassignment. It removes v3's explicit confounding/interpretability limitations and weight-drift explanation for weak gradient correlations. The downstream nonsignificance finding and sequential-learning qualification remain.

D1.justification: v4 newly documents Tulu input-length filtering, additional corpus subsamples, and Rotated-MNIST training details. It revises the prediction-epoch specification and explains task-level MIR-T retrieval. Conversely, the explicit OLMo checkpoint links and dataset/model license paragraph are removed. Most software, LoRA, and replay details remain.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for Pythia, Pile, OLMo2, and additional continual-learning approaches, including Roth et al. and Buzzega et al. It removes references associated with the earlier error-editing framing and some other citations. The central positioning relative to example-forgetting prediction and data selection remains stable.

P1.justification: The introduction and analysis narrative are extensively rewritten. Section 2 reorganizes model/data descriptions, Section 3 adopts a formulation–comparison–interpretation structure, and similarity-method details move into Appendix C. The appendices expand and reorganize, while an Impact Statement replaces the standalone limitations discussion.

P2.justification: v4 changes the document from predominantly single-column to two-column layout and extensively rearranges displays. It adds binary-forgetting, model-scaling, and synthetic-experiment figures; expands the prediction diagram to illustrate replay; restructures Table 2; and adds replay bars. The OLMo-1B heatmap moves from the main text to the appendix rather than being removed.

improvement.justification: Binary-forgetting evaluation, matched model comparisons, and controlled rotation/depth experiments strengthen validation and interpretation of the existing low-rank finding. However, the established practical conclusions change little: downstream accuracy results and their nonsignificance remain unchanged. Removal of useful limitation and reproducibility information partly offsets the added evidence, making the net quality improvement limited.
